integrity: The source transfer map becomes a global bidiagonal linear map on a chain. The proof reconstructs every facet slack, computes its Euclidean gradient norm after transfer, and uses the simplex identity that the facet slacks sum to one. Equal facet distances give the unique incenter and exact radius. Endpoint derivative signs prove strict interior improvement, and the two-dimensional optimum follows from strict convexity. Finite linear-program replay is corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns the diagonal parameter path in the continuous marked-poset family for a chain with endpoint markings zero and one. It does not give the inradius for arbitrary marked posets or arbitrary parameter vectors. For dimensions at least three it proves an interior maximizer exists but does not claim a closed form or uniqueness.
title: Uniform chain interpolants have an exact Euclidean inradius profile
